source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine Cooling, p.6K-1

procedures.title: Coolant level: check
steps: Check coolant level only with the engine cool (especially with air conditioning); opening the cap on a hot system can cause serious injury.
Downflow radiator: keep the level 1 inch below the bottom of the filler neck when cold, or at the bottom of the neck when warm.
Crossflow radiator: keep the level 3 inches below the bottom of the filler neck when cold.
If coolant is lost repeatedly, check the pressure cap and its seat for sealing, and look for loose hose connections, bad hoses and gasket leaks.

specs.what: safe coolant temperature with 15 lb. cap

notes: Overfilling hurts the cap's ability to seal.
Removing or loosening the cap drops pressure to atmospheric and coolant above 212°F flashes to steam, blowing coolant out of the upper hose and top tank.
Running above water's normal boiling point is fine as long as the cold coolant level is right.
Radiator service is in Section 13; fan shroud replacement in Section 11. The pressure cap has a relief valve that vents to the overflow (see figure 1 in the manual).

The water pump (ball bearing, centrifugal vane impeller) needs no care except keeping the top air vent and bottom drain holes clear; overhaul is in Section 6K of the Passenger Chassis Overhaul Manual.

procedures.title: Cooling system checks
steps: Radiator restriction: warm the engine, shut it off and feel the radiator; it should be hot at the top and warm at the bottom with an even rise between. Cold spots mean clogged sections.
Water pump: run the engine and squeeze the upper hose; you should feel a pressure surge. Also check the pump vent hole is not plugged.
notes: A bad head gasket can let exhaust into the coolant, forming acids that damage radiator and engine.
